speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned waking up frightened; can you tell me if you ever stop breathing, snore loudly, or kick your legs during these episodes? Also, are these events happening more often at night or during the day?

speaker: Patient
text: 8-year-old female. The patient has been experiencing difficulty sleeping for the past 2 months, with episodes of waking up frightened occurring one to two times per week. During these episodes, she yells and cries but does not seem confused after waking and can be consoled by her parents. The following day, she appears more tired than usual.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Night terrors.

I have reviewed your symptoms of waking up frightened with crying but remaining confused and consolable, which distinguishes this from typical nightmares. Given the frequency and the resulting daytime fatigue, are there any known family members who experience similar sleep disturbances?
